content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?Commemorative Air Force's PostCommemorative Air Force Verified accountSeptember 16, 2025 · Shared with PublicOn September 16, 1951, Sky King first appeared on American television and instantly captured the imagination of aviation fans across the country. Viewers tuned in on that Sunday afternoon to hear the booming voice of the announcer and to see the opening shot of a twin-engine plane sweeping in low across the desert with the promise that, “Out of the clear blue of the western sky comes, Sky King!” The story of Sky King began earlier on the radio, where Schuyler “Sky” King debuted in 1946. Listeners followed his adventures as a former military aviator turned rancher who used his airplane, the Songbird, to battle rustlers, chase criminals, and rescue those in trouble. The program not only offered exciting weekly episodes but also the kind of premiums that made kids feel part of the adventure, from secret code decoders to glow-in-the-dark rings. It was a world that fired the imagination and made flight seem like the ultimate pathway to freedom.When the series moved to television, Kirby Grant stepped into the role of Sky King, joined by his niece Penny, played by Gloria Winters, and occasionally his nephew Clipper, played by Ron Hagerthy. The family lived at the Flying Crown Ranch, but the real star of the show was always the airplane. Early episodes featured a Cessna T-50 “Bamboo Bomber,” a rugged twin-engine trainer that still holds a special place in aviation history. Soon after, Sky began flying the sleeker and more modern Cessna 310, which became the most recognizable version of Songbird. The 310 brought a new level of glamour and speed to the series, and its sharp lines made it one of the most beloved television aircraft of the era.More than seventy years later, Sky King remains a cultural landmark for aviation enthusiasts. It represents a time when flight still carried the aura of romance and discovery, when television made heroes out of pilots, and when a plane could become as famous as its pilot. Were you a Sky King fan?All reactions:2.3K410 comments203 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Top fanMike CzervinskeRemember it well. Neither plane replaced my love for the Bonanza, but the 310 came in 3rd with Penny second.30w4Thomas Jerry ShanahanBack in the 60's my dad had two sets of floats for the bomber, he owned two planes one on floats and the other wheels and straight skis...they called this one Bushmaster31w7Lewis JohnsonI recognized the plane, immediately! On Saturday following "Fury," "Rin Tin Tin", Superman, Space Patrol and Commando Cody!30w4Jerry CookYup!!!! I was a young kid living in Mattoon IL when I began watching Sky King!!! And it was still when he was flying the Bamboo Bomber! I recall being disappointed when the C-310 made it's debut because I was so enamored with the T-50. Many years later, I was a San Diego sailor and I recall once hitch hiking to LA via I-5. A driver picked me up and we began talking airplanes. He was pleasantly shocked when I mentioned my love of the "Bamboo Bomber"......because by then (1969 ) it had drifted into obscurity and nobody remembered it anymore!I believe it was that airplane that truly ignited my fascination and passion for flying! By 18, I had earned my Private Pilot's license, and then upon returning from the Navy, I earned my Commercial, Instrument, Multi-engine, and Flight Instructor certificates.31w13Jeremy NicholsI was thrilled when, flying into Phoenix or the first time, I learned the airport was really called “Sky Harbor.”30w2Eugene FodorI started a career in aviation because of this show and 15,000 hours later , I retired. Great life.31w4Joe LairdThere were three programs I looked forward to watching growing up in the Chicago area. Captain Kangaroo, Garfield Goose, and Sky King30w2View 1 replyGary CurranI still love the joke I heard about the Bamboo Bomber, and I don't know if it's true or not, but it could be.Apparently a Cessna T-50 was on approach into a bigger airport, was established on final, and they got a call from the tower to ask how fast they were going. The pilot replied something like 70 mph. The tower said he had another, faster airplane on final behind him and asked if he could speed up to 90 knots.The T-50 pilot replied 'Yes, we can do that, but we have to put that landing gear back up!'30w2Donald HarenRemembering Sky King! When I was a small boy I always watched the show. It was instrumental in helping me be driven to become a pilot. I earned my private license at the age of 17 and later added my commercial and instrument ratings. Always wanted to live like Sky with a ranch and private airstrip. I didn't have that but I did own a Piper Cherokee for a few years. Now I am 77 and no longer able to fly but I have so many great memories!30w2Wayne AndersonBack in the 1950's we had heroes. Mine was Sky King and Mike Nelson. I became a pilot and scuba diver. Kids don't have heroes anymore.
